target_pattern: Use ir a + place and ir a + place + a + infinitive to express movement and purpose, and combine it with querer, poder, and tener que.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Translating to one-to-one and getting stuck when a sentence has two to ideas (go to X / to do Y).
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish motion uses ir a + place, and purpose uses a second a + infinitive.
natural_examples: Tengo que ir al banco hoy.
Voy a la tienda a comprar pan.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Voy a la tienda. -> make it a question (tú).
Base: Quiero ir al banco. -> make it negative.
Base: Tengo que ir al supermercado. -> change yo to nosotros.
Base: ¿Puedes ir a la farmacia? -> answer no in full sentence.
Base: Voy a la tienda a comprar pan. -> change product to leche.
Base: Quiero ir al parque. -> add purpose: to run.
Base: Puedo ir al cine hoy. -> move to tomorrow.
Base: Tengo que ir a la oficina. -> turn into question.
Base: ¿Quieres ir al gimnasio conmigo? -> answer yes in full sentence.
Base: Voy a la biblioteca. -> change destination to plural people (ellos) and place escuela.
Base: Tengo que ir a la tienda a comprar huevos. -> make it negative.
Base: ¿Puedes ir al banco ahora? -> change ahora to después.
Base: Quiero ir al hospital. -> change to past (I went).
Base: Puedo ir a la playa el sábado. -> change to inability.
Base: Voy al supermercado. -> expand with purpose to buy vegetables.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the most natural pattern and write in Spanish.
prompts: I am going to the store. (voy vs quiero ir)
I want to go to the store. (voy vs quiero ir)
I can go to the store. (puedo ir vs voy)
I have to go to the store. (tengo que ir vs puedo ir)
Can you go to the bank? (¿puedes ir...? vs ¿quieres ir...?)
Do you want to go to the beach? (¿quieres ir...? vs ¿tienes que ir...?)
I am going to the store to buy bread. (ir a + lugar + a + infinitivo vs para)
I have to go to the pharmacy to buy medicine. (tengo que ir a ... a comprar ...)
I cannot go to the office today. (no puedo ir vs no quiero ir) meaning = ability problem.
I do not want to go to the office today. (no quiero ir vs no puedo ir) meaning = desire problem.
